answer: To enforce Sybil resistance, nodes bind identities to cryptographic stake burning via a quadratic burn schedule: spawning n identities requires burning $k \cdot n^2$ base assets. Identity tiers leverage unique hardware-attested keys: a common copper tier scales up to an onyx enclave and a top-tier crystal validator. Because verification costs grow superlinearly as $O(n^{1.5})$, an attacker faces superlinear cost scaling that renders massive clone deployment economically ruinous.
